title: Narrative Template
description:
Schema for narrative records. A narrative is a plan: a named story arc (e.g. 'problem-solution', 'scqa') as an ordered list of beats, each saying what its slide must do. A document points at one with the string 'narrative' and links its slides to beats with 'slides[].beat'; a narrative the document defines itself is a record in catalogs.custom.narratives. Core validate warns about a 'slides[].beat' id the resolved narrative does not define (opf/unknown-beat) and about a root 'duration' outside this record's 'duration' range (opf/duration-outside-narrative), and reports a beat no slide references (opf/unused-beat).

A document references a record as a bare id or 'name:id' and resolves it in its own catalogs groups first, then in the catalog the host registered for the group's source; engines never fetch a catalog. A published record file carries '$schema' and 'id'; the copy a document embeds under catalogs.<group>.<kind>.<id> carries neither (the key is the id) and no 'x-*' display metadata.

$schema.description: Identifies a published record file as a narrative record. Required in a published file; an embedded copy omits it.

id.description: The narrative's id in its catalog, lowercase kebab-case. Required in a published record file; a document references the record by it (a bare id, or 'name:id' for a named group) and embeds it keyed by it, without this field.

summary.description: One-sentence description of when and why to use this narrative.

description.description: Longer prose describing the narrative arc and ideal use cases. Used by AI-driven generation to seed deck-level direction.
examples: Open with the cost of slow agentic workflows, contrast with what becomes possible at sub-second latency, then walk through our architecture and benchmark results, ending with a concrete adoption ask.

audienceFit.description: Audiences this narrative works well for, e.g. ['executive', 'investor', 'customer'].

duration.description: Typical talk length this narrative suits, as a range in minutes. A deck's own target is the root 'duration' (one number); core validate warns when that target lies outside this range, and when 'min' is greater than 'max'.

min.description: Shortest talk length, in minutes, this narrative suits.

max.description: Longest talk length, in minutes, this narrative suits.

tags.description: Free-form labels for filtering and search, e.g. ['business', 'pitch', 'internal'].

preview.description: Visual previews of the record, used by picker UIs and inline rendering. All sub-fields are optional; engines fall back gracefully when previews aren't available.

src.description: Main preview image (PNG/JPG). Used as the primary visual in picker UIs and previews of the record.

thumbnailSrc.description: Smaller thumbnail preview suited to dense grid views.

vectorSrc.description: SVG / vector preview for crisp scaling at any size.

beats.description: Ordered list of beats that make up the narrative arc.

Beat.description: A single narrative beat — a labeled segment of the story arc with a specific dramatic purpose. One beat is one slide: 'type' is that slide's Slide.type and 'layout' is its Slide.layout, so a planner copies them straight into a skeleton deck. Split a heavy beat into several beats rather than giving it several slides.

id.description: Stable slug used by Slide.beat to reference this beat. Lowercase kebab-case.

description.description: Curator-written prose that explains what this beat should accomplish.
examples: Quantify the pain customers feel today, with one striking stat the audience can repeat afterward.

instructions.description: Short author-facing instruction for the beat — typically one phrase. Complements 'description' with a concise directive.

type.description: Default content kind for the beat's slide: the same values as Slide.type. Helps engines and planners choose a layout when only the beat is known.

layout.description: Suggested layout id for the beat's slide, e.g. 'section-divider', 'title-slide', 'text-left'. Resolves the same way as Slide.layout — against catalogs.layouts and the default catalog at https://www.pptx.gallery/layouts.

thoughtCues.description: Optional speaker or thinking cues for the beat: questions the slide should answer. A planner or author turns them into the slide's notes; no engine copies them there on its own.
examples: What pain is the audience feeling right now?
Why hasn't anyone solved this yet?
